user.title: Ember
user.description: Set up Ember, then add thermostats to it.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Ember is already set up. Add thermostats to it instead.

init.title: Ember
init.description: Settings shared by all thermostats. Changes on each page are kept until you choose Save and close.

data_description.entity: Optional. A person, a zone, or an occupancy or presence sensor. While nobody is home, thermostats use the away temperature of their preset. Without one, Ember treats the home as always occupied.

presets.title: Presets
presets.description: Each preset's temperature while someone is home and while nobody is.

data_description.away: Used while the presence entity says nobody is home. Without a presence entity, only the first temperature is used.

data.min_switch_time: Minimum switch on or off time

data_description.kp: Output in % for each degree below the target.
data_description.interval: How often the output is worked out again.
data_description.cycle: Switches are on for the output's share of each cycle.
data_description.min_switch_time: Shorter on or off periods are skipped.

data_description.sensor_timeout: A temperature sensor that hasn't reported for this long is treated as broken. Battery sensors that only report changes need a few hours.
data_description.fallback_output: Valve opening or switch share used while the sensor is broken.

data_description.open_delay: How long a window is open before heating stops.

data_description.timeout: How long Ember leaves a device alone after it's changed outside Ember.

central_heating.title: Central heating
central_heating.description: Ticked thermostats count towards the central heating demand entities, for example to run a boiler or heat pump. This sets the same option as Part of central heating on each thermostat.

data_description.area: Optional. The device is placed in this area.
data_description.name: The name of the device, for example Radiator. The thermostat is listed as the area followed by this name.
data_description.heaters: One or more switches, or one or more climate entities such as TRVs. With valve entities, choose one climate entity.
data_description.opening_degree: Optional. With both valve entities, Ember sets the TRV's valve directly. Without them, Ember passes the target temperature to the TRVs.
data_description.window_sensor: Optional. Heating stops while it's open.

data_description.area: Optional. The device is placed in this area.

data_description.opening_degree: Optional. With both valve entities, Ember sets the TRV's valve directly. Without them, Ember passes the target temperature to the TRVs.
data_description.window_sensor: Optional. Heating stops while it's open.

data_description.central_heating: Counts towards the demand entities of Ember's central heating, for example to run a boiler or heat pump. You can also change this for all thermostats at once on the Central heating page of Ember's settings.
data_description.use_central_presets: Turn off to set this thermostat's own preset temperatures.
data_description.use_central_control: Turn off to set this thermostat's own PID and cycle settings.

error.mixed_heaters: Choose switches or a climate entity, not both.
error.valve_pair: Choose both valve entities, or neither.
error.valve_needs_climate: Valve entities need exactly one climate entity as heater.

stale_sensor.description: {sensor} has no usable reading. Thermostat {thermostat} runs at the fallback output until it reports again.
